fullPassage:
The Science Behind the Mona Lisa

Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for which he is famous. One example is the Mona Lisa. This painting utilizes da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his magnificent artistic skills. Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the perception that the eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting. Additionally, da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting. The farther the object is, the smaller the scale, the more subtle the colors, and the less detailed the outlines are.

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most (A)[intelligent / innocent] painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an (B)[accomplished / abandoned] scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually (C)[exclusive / excessive]. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
① intelligent - accomplished - exclusive ← 정답

② innocent(순수한): '가장 지적인 화가'이므로 intelligent가 적절

③ abandoned(버려진): '뛰어난 과학자'이므로 accomplished가 적절

④ excessive(과도한): 'mutually exclusive(상호 배타적인)'가 적절
det.tip: intelligent(지적인), accomplished(뛰어난, 숙련된), mutually exclusive(상호 배타적인)

questions.passage: During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the (A)[outstanding / ordinary] masterpieces for which he is famous. One example is the Mona Lisa. This painting (B)[utilizes / undermines] da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his (C)[magnificent / minimal] artistic skills.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
① ordinary(평범한): '뛰어난 걸작'이므로 outstanding이 적절

② undermines(약화시키다): 과학적 지식을 '활용한다'이므로 utilizes가 적절

③ minimal(최소한의): '훌륭한 예술적 기량'이므로 magnificent가 적절

④ outstanding - utilizes - magnificent ← 정답

questions.passage: This painting utilizes da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his magnificent artistic skills. Da Vinci was (A)[fascinated / frustrated] by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to (B)[determine / distribute] the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's (C)[mysterious / mechanical] smile. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
① frustrated(좌절한): 미소의 형성에 '매료되었다'이므로 fascinated가 적절

② distribute(분배하다): 신경의 기원을 '알아내다'이므로 determine이 적절

③ fascinated - determine - mysterious ← 정답

④ mechanical(기계적인): 모나리자의 '신비로운' 미소이므로 mysterious가 적절

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most ①<u>intelligent</u> painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic ②<u>masterpieces</u>, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually ③<u>inclusive</u>. Rather, one was seen as ④<u>informing</u> upon the other.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ inclusive → exclusive (상호 배타적인 것으로 인식되지 않았다)
det.analysis:
✅ ① intelligent(지적인): 가장 지적인 화가 — 적절

✅ ② masterpieces(걸작): 예술적 걸작으로 유명 — 적절

❌ ③ inclusive → exclusive: '상호 배타적인(mutually exclusive)' 것으로 인식되지 않았다가 원문 ← 정답

✅ ④ informing(알려주는): 서로에게 정보를 주는 — 적절
det.tip: mutually exclusive(상호 배타적인) ↔ mutually inclusive(상호 포용적인)

questions.passage: Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that ①<u>control</u> each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him to ②<u>produce</u> Mona Lisa's mysterious smile. He also carefully ③<u>positioned</u> the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly ④<u>fixed</u>, while the eyes still face the viewer.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ fixed → turned (각 요소가 약간 돌아가 있도록)
det.analysis:
✅ ① control(제어하다): 각 얼굴 근육을 제어하는 신경 — 적절

✅ ② produce(만들어내다): 신비로운 미소를 만들어냄 — 적절

✅ ③ positioned(배치하다): 몸통, 머리, 눈을 신중히 배치 — 적절

❌ ④ fixed → turned: 각 요소가 약간 '돌아가 있다(turned)'가 원문 ← 정답

questions.passage: Hence, we have the perception that the eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting. Additionally, da Vinci created the ①<u>illusion</u> of depth in the painting. The farther the object is, the ②<u>larger</u> the scale, the more ③<u>subtle</u> the colors, and the less ④<u>detailed</u> the outlines are.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② larger → smaller (멀수록 크기가 더 작아진다)
det.analysis:
✅ ① illusion(환상): 깊이의 환상을 만듦 — 적절

❌ ② larger → smaller: 멀수록 크기가 더 '작아진다(smaller)'가 원문 ← 정답

✅ ③ subtle(미묘한): 멀수록 색상이 더 미묘해짐 — 적절

✅ ④ detailed(세밀한): 덜 세밀해진다(less detailed) — 적절

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an accomplished scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually __________. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 배타적인(exclusive) — 예술과 과학은 상호 배타적으로 인식되지 않았다
det.analysis:
① essential(필수적인): '상호 필수적'은 문맥상 Rather 이하의 반전 구조와 맞지 않음 — 부적절

② exclusive(배타적인): mutually exclusive, 서로 배타적으로 인식되지 않았다 ← 정답

③ extensive(광범위한): 문맥에 맞지 않음 — 부적절

④ expensive(비싼): 문맥과 무관 — 부적절
det.tip: mutually exclusive = 상호 배타적인 (하나를 택하면 다른 것은 안 됨)

questions.passage: This painting utilizes da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his magnificent artistic skills. Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in __________ allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 해부학(anatomy) — 얼굴 근육과 신경에 대한 관심
det.analysis:
① astronomy(천문학): 얼굴 근육/신경과 무관 — 부적절

② archaeology(고고학): 문맥과 무관 — 부적절

③ anatomy(해부학): 근육, 신경, 얼굴 각 부분의 움직임 연구와 직결 ← 정답

④ architecture(건축학): 문맥과 무관 — 부적절

questions.passage: This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile. He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the perception that the eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting. Additionally, da Vinci created the __________ of depth in the painting. The farther the object is, the smaller the scale, the more subtle the colors, and the less detailed the outlines are.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
① illusion(환상, 착시): 그림에 깊이의 환상을 만듦 ← 정답

② influence(영향): '깊이의 영향'은 부자연스러움 — 부적절

③ illustration(삽화, 설명): '깊이의 삽화'는 부자연스러움 — 부적절

④ implication(함축): '깊이의 함축'은 부자연스러움 — 부적절
det.tip: illusion of depth = 깊이의 착시/환상 (원근법 기법)

questions.passage: Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most intelligent painters in the history of art. Although he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he was also an <u>accomplished</u> scientist. During the Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as mutually exclusive. Rather, one was seen as informing upon the other.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 accomplished와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
① ambitious(야심찬): accomplished와 의미 다름

② accidental(우연한): accomplished와 의미 다름

③ acknowledged(인정받는): 유사하지만 '숙련된'이 더 정확

④ skilled(숙련된): accomplished와 유사한 의미 ← 정답

questions.passage: Da Vinci was <u>fascinated</u> by how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face to determine the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce Mona Lisa's mysterious smile.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 fascinated와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
① frightened(겁먹은): fascinated와 의미 다름

② captivated(매혹된): fascinated와 유사한 의미 ← 정답

③ frustrated(좌절한): fascinated와 의미 다름

④ exhausted(지친): fascinated와 의미 다름

questions.passage: He also carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face the viewer. Hence, we have the <u>perception</u> that the eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at us, even when we are not directly in front of the painting.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 perception과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
① permission(허가): perception과 의미 다름

② perfection(완벽함): perception과 의미 다름

③ impression(인상, 느낌): perception과 유사한 의미 ← 정답

④ profession(직업): perception과 의미 다름

questions.passage: In fact, it was largely through a scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the <u>outstanding</u> masterpieces for which he is famous. One example is the Mona Lisa. This painting utilizes da Vinci's scientific knowledge as well as his magnificent artistic skills.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 outstanding과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
① mediocre(평범한, 그저 그런): outstanding과 반대 의미 ← 정답

② unusual(특이한): outstanding의 반의어 아님

③ unknown(알려지지 않은): outstanding의 반의어 아님

④ unfinished(미완성의): outstanding의 반의어 아님

questions.passage: Additionally, da Vinci created the illusion of depth in the painting. The farther the object is, the smaller the scale, the more <u>subtle</u> the colors, and the less detailed the outlines are.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 subtle과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
① simple(단순한): subtle의 반의어 아님

② secret(비밀의): subtle의 반의어 아님

③ smooth(매끄러운): subtle의 반의어 아님

④ striking(뚜렷한, 눈에 띄는): subtle과 반대 의미 ← 정답
det.tip: subtle(미묘한, 감지하기 어려운) ↔ striking(뚜렷한, 눈에 띄는)

questions.passage:
(A) Da Vinci was fascinated by how a smile begins to <u>form</u>. So, he evaluated every possible movement of each part of the face.

(B) Please fill out this application <u>form</u> and submit it by Friday.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 form의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은? (A) (B)

det.analysis:
① 형성하다 - 형태: (A)는 '형성되다'이고 (B)는 '양식'이므로 부적절

② 형성되다 - 양식 ← 정답

③ 구성하다 - 양식: (A)는 '형성되다'이므로 부적절

④ 형성되다 - 형태: (B)는 '양식'이므로 부적절
det.tip: form은 동사(형성되다/구성하다)와 명사(형태/양식/서식) 여러 의미로 쓰인다.

det.korean: evaluate: 어떤 것의 가치, 질, 중요성을 판단하거나 평가하다
det.analysis:
① perceive(인식하다): '평가하다'의 의미 아님

② produce(생산하다): '평가하다'의 의미 아님

det.korean: be + p.p.: were not perceived (인식되지 않았다)
det.analysis:
① perceived(과거분사): were not perceived — 수동태 ← 정답

② perceiving(현재분사): 수동태가 필요하므로 부적절

③ perception(명사): 동사 자리에 명사 부적절

④ perceptive(형용사): 문맥상 수동태가 필요 — 부적절
det.tip: be + p.p. (수동태): were not perceived = 인식되지 않았다

det.analysis:
① detailing(현재분사/동명사): 보어 자리에 형용사 필요 — 부적절

② detailed(세밀한, 형용사): the less detailed the outlines are ← 정답

③ details(명사 복수/동사 3인칭): 보어 자리에 형용사 필요 — 부적절

④ detailedly(부사 형태): 실제 사용되지 않는 형태 — 부적절
det.tip: the + 비교급 ~, the + 비교급 ~ (더 ~할수록, 더 ~하다). detailed = 형용사(세밀한)
